pageCache.pageTitle: Trinity Oaks CofE Primary School | Acorns Pre-school
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Trinity Oaks CofE Primary School and Acorns Pre-school
‘Where acorns flourish into mighty oaks’
Welcome to our school
We are proud to be a vibrant, inclusive and ambitious Christian community where every child is known, valued and encouraged to thrive. Our dedicated staff work tirelessly to provide a rich and engaging curriculum, alongside a wide range of opportunities that support both academic success and personal development.
There are many wonderful things happening here each day, from inspiring classroom learning to creative arts, sporting achievements and meaningful community experiences. We hope that, as you explore our website, you gain a real sense of the energy, care and aspiration that define our school.
We warmly invite you to visit us and see our school in action. There is no substitute for experiencing first-hand the positive relationships, high expectations and welcoming atmosphere that make our school such a special place to learn and grow.
We look forward to meeting you.
Mrs Elizabeth WoodsHeadteacher
Since joining the Diocese of Southwark in September 2014, our school has served more than 220 pupils each year, aged three to eleven. From Acorns Pre-school through to Year 6, we offer a rich and inclusive curriculum designed to challenge, inspire and prepare children for the future.
Our core values – Respectful, Kind and Compassionate, Thankful, Resilient and Aspirational – are lived out daily in every classroom, in worship, in our approach to wellbeing and in the relationships between pupils, staff and parents.
Our Vision and Values
Relationships are at the heart of all that we do. As a small school, every individual is known and cherished. We focus on building and maintaining positive relationships with all pupils and their families.
Trinity Oaks is a place where compassion and rigour go hand in hand, enabling all acorns to flourish into mighty oaks. Academic success does not come at the expense of a caring environment; it thrives because of it.
‘Rooted in God’s love and Christian values, we are a school who treasure each individual, enabling them to flourish and achieve.’
Our academic results and newsletters reflect a vibrant, high-achieving school community where there is always something exciting taking place. This creates a dynamic and ambitious environment for all to achieve.
Our Pre-School, Acorns, provides a warm, nurturing and stimulating environment where our youngest children take their very first steps in education.
In Acorns, we focus on building strong foundations through play, exploration and high-quality interactions. Children are supported to develop their communication and language skills, grow in confidence and independence, and begin to form positive relationships with others.
Our experienced staff create a safe and engaging setting where every child is valued as an individual. Through a carefully planned curriculum, children are encouraged to be curious, active learners, developing the key skills they need as they prepare for Reception and beyond.
As part of the Trinity Oaks community, children in Acorns benefit from a seamless transition into school life, becoming familiar with routines, expectations and the wider environment from an early stage.
We are proud to offer a caring and inspiring start to each child’s educational journey.
Visit our new Instagram page to get a glimpse inside Acorns
Christian distinctiveness
As a Church School, our Christian distinctiveness is rooted in our vision inspired by the Church of England’s call to be “Deeply Christian, serving the common good.” We embed our Christian values in everything we do, including our curriculum, worship, behaviour and relationships. Our Christian character is not simply what we say, but what we live. Our priority is that every child feels safe, valued, heard and loved, guided by our values as we strive for excellence and compassion in equal measure.
We also understand the increasing demands on families. To support this, we provide high-quality wraparound care, a dedicated home-school link worker and a close-knit community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Key Stage 1 (5-7years) | Explore Learning Opportunities - Enroll Today — Trinity Oaks CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Key Stage 1 (5-7years)
Key Stage 1 Curriculum
The Key Stage 1 (KS 1) curriculum for Years 1 and 2 (5, 6 and 7 year olds) is carefully planned to further develop foundational skills and build on prior knowledge and skills learnt in the Early Years Foundation stage (EYFS).
Our skills-based curriculum meets the requirements of the National Curriculum in England and this forms the core knowledge, skills and understanding that pupils need to acquire by the end of the Key Stage.
Learning in Key Stage 1 takes place within the context of learning themes (topics). These are chosen to appeal to pupils and build on their interests. Learning in this enriched, cross-curricular way helps children to make explicit links between different areas of their learning. Each day the children have English and mathematics lessons and we teach them to apply the skills learnt in these core subjects across the curriculum. In this way they practise, consolidate and embed their learning.
Wherever possible, pupils learn from first-hand experiences, working in the classroom as well as outside, making the most of opportunities that arise from our beautiful rural setting.
Phonics is implemented, using Phonics Shed, at the end of Pre-School, throughout Reception and Key Stage 1 to develop early reading and writing skills. Consistent teaching and regular assessment, alongside focused resources, enables children to secure fundamental skills. Children learn to read accurately and fluently, with good comprehension.
The structure of these lessons are consistent across the phases and provide opportunities for children to revisit, learn, practise and apply new sounds to develop their segmenting and blending skills.
Children are expected to complete this programme by the end of the Autumn Term in Year 2. Individual children will be supported to continue the targeted learning of phonics, on an intervention basis. This will be continued into Key Stage 2, where need requires.
In 2025 our Year 1 cohort all achieved their phonics screen check - we had 100% pass mark.
If you would like to learn more about our curriculum, please contact us.
“My children have a real love of learning which is nurtured and developed at the school. They are very encouraging and supportive school. I’m very glad that my children are happy!”

pageCache.pageTitle: Key Stage 2 (7-11 years) | Empower Young Learners Today — Trinity Oaks CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Key Stage 2 (7-11years)
Key Stage 2 Curriculum
The Key Stage 2 curriculum is carefully planned to build on prior knowledge and skills learnt in KS1 and to prepare children for their secondary education.
Our curriculum is based on and meets the requirements of the National Curriculum in England and this forms the core knowledge, skills and understanding that pupils need to acquire by the end of the Key Stage.
Learning in Key Stage 2 takes place within the context of over-arching topics or themes. These are designed to engage pupils and develop their understanding of different contexts. Learning in this enriched, cross-curricular way helps children to make explicit links between different areas of their learning.
Each day the children have English and mathematics lessons. In English there is an increased focus on spelling, punctuation and grammar and in mathematics on learning tables and developing reasoning skills. We teach the children to apply the skills learnt in these core subjects across the curriculum. In this way they practise, consolidate and embed their learning. Pupils have computer science lessons and receive regular guidance on how to stay safe on line.
The curriculum is linked to whole school events and festivals through the year such as learning about Diwali or Remembrance Sunday. Wherever possible pupils learn from first-hand experiences, working outdoors as well as in the classroom.
If you would like to learn more about our curriculum, please contact us.
“My children have a real love of learning which is nurtured and developed at the school. They are a very encouraging and supportive school. I’m very glad that my children are happy!”

pageCache.text:
PE and School Sport Funding
At Trinity Oaks C of E Primary School we recognise the importance of high quality PE and School Sport in the life of the school
The school has an important role in providing pupils with the confidence and skills for lifelong participation in physical activity as this will lead to better long term health
It is recognised that physical activity makes a valuable contribution to pupils’ health and well being
Research shows that physical activity can improve academic success
School sport contributes to pupils’ ability to work as a team and demonstrate leadership. It helps to build character and embed the values of fairness and respect
Local competition helps us to work with other schools, raise the profile of the school and develop links with sporting organisations in the local community.
To provide a supportive environment and a range of opportunities to increase the physical activity levels of the whole school and improve the health and well-being of pupils, staff and parents/carers
To keep under review our policy for physical activity so that it is appropriate for older pupils as the school grows.
The intended outcomes of this policy are:
To increase pupils’ knowledge, understanding, experience and attitudes towards physical activity
To provide positive sporting role models and consistent messages in school about physical activity both within and outside the taught curriculum
To improve pupil’s physical fitness, behaviour, self-esteem, confidence and ability to work with one another.
Our PE, School Sports and Physical Activity (PESSPA) Funding Provision and Impact report for 2024-25 can be read here.

pageCache.pageTitle: Whole School Curriculum | Discover Quality Learning - Enroll Today — Trinity Oaks CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Whole School Curriculum
At Trinity Oaks, our curriculum is carefully designed to be interlinked, meaningful and rich in context. Each subject connects thoughtfully with others, enabling pupils to deepen their understanding and make purposeful links in their learning.
We place a strong emphasis on developing communication and language. Through exposure to high-quality texts, ambitious vocabulary and purposeful discussion, pupils are supported to articulate their ideas clearly and confidently.
In the early years and Key Stage 1, we prioritise the development of strong foundational skills. We ensure that every child builds secure knowledge in reading, writing and mathematics, alongside the social and communication skills they need to thrive. This provides a firm platform as they move through the school and prepare for their next steps.
Our curriculum is designed to engage and inspire. Lessons are planned to capture pupils’ interests while maintaining high expectations for all. We believe that every child can achieve highly, and we are committed to ensuring that outcomes reflect this ambition.
At Trinity Oaks, we are proud of a curriculum that not only equips pupils with essential knowledge and skills, but also fosters curiosity, confidence and a lifelong love of learning.
Useful summer term information for parents can be found here.
We place relationships at the heart of everything we do and every child is recognised as a unique individual and is provided with equitable, first-hand learning experiences, which help underpin the teaching of basic skills, knowledge, concepts, values, and attitudes. Every child is provided with an ambitious and challenging curriculum suited to their individual needs.
The intent of the curriculum at Trinity Oaks C of E Primary school is to provide relevant and ‘stickable’ linked learning opportunities where pupils are excited and engaged in authentic learning experiences, within a flexible timetable. Core and foundation subjects are mapped and interlinked to provide immersive learning opportunities across curriculum areas, building upon prior skills and knowledge. Therefore, they are not afraid to make mistakes and learn from being ‘in the pit’, building resilience and developing creative and critical thinking. We have high aspirations for our children with expected outcomes in line with or higher than Surrey average attainment percentages.
Intrinsic motivation plays a central role in this approach. By fostering a deep connection to what they are learning, we encourage children to find joy and satisfaction in the process itself rather than just external rewards. This is enhanced through exploration of their passions and interests, helping each child discover what excites them and drives their curiosity. When children are motivated by their own passions, they develop a lifelong love for learning that extends beyond the classroom and into all areas of their lives. This personal investment not only boosts their confidence but also reinforces the value of perseverance, self-direction, and intrinsic success.
The curriculum at Trinity Oaks C of E Primary school is to not only develop academic skills and knowledge, but to improve children’s life chances and equip them for the wider world through developing self-worth, kindness and compassion, respect, and integrity. This is underpinned by high expectations for behaviour and a focus on developing relationships between self, others and curriculum.
Children come to school feeling a sense of pride for their school as a community and are enthusiastic towards the many opportunities that are available to them, both in and outside of the classroom.

pageCache.pageTitle: Treetops Wraparound Care | Discover Quality Childcare - Enroll Today — Trinity Oaks CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Treetops Wraparound Care
High quality out-of-hours childcare to support parents and carers
Treetops provides a range of engaging and creative activities in a safe environment, led by qualified and professional school staff. Treetops is open to children who are on roll at Trinity Oaks Primary School, from Pre-school to Year 6 for Breakfast Club and from Reception to Year 6 for After School Club.
Breakfast Club is open from 7.45am – 8.40am during term time. Children are served a choice of cereal and/or toast with juice or milk. Breakfast is served at 8:10am.
After School Club is open from 3.10pm – 6.00pm during term time. Children are served a snack such as beans on toast, pasta or filled wraps. Snack is served from 4.10pm - 4.40pm.
Charges for the 2026-27 academic year are:
Breakfast Club £6.75 per child
After School Club £15.50 per child
All parents/carers must complete the registration form for each child attending Treetops. Registration is free and children do not need to be re-registered each year.
We accept payment with childcare vouchers and the Government tax-free childcare scheme.
Once registered, you can make block bookings in advance or ad hoc bookings for certain days – as the need arises.

pageCache.pageTitle: Creative Arts | Explore Creative Arts—Inspire Creativity Today — Trinity Oaks CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Creative Arts
Our school places a high value on the creative arts as a vital part of a broad and balanced curriculum. We believe that opportunities in art, music, and performance enable pupils to express themselves, build confidence, and develop imagination and resilience.
Each class from Year 1 to Year 6 benefits from weekly creative arts lessons delivered by our skilled Higher Level Teaching Assistant. This ensures consistency, expertise, and a real sense of excitement in every session. Pupils engage in a wide range of experiences, from visual arts to performance, allowing them to explore and develop their individual talents.
Our music curriculum is particularly strong, offering pupils rich and engaging opportunities to perform, compose, and appreciate music from a range of genres and traditions. We aim to inspire a lifelong love of music while developing technical skills and creativity.
We have high aspirations for all pupils in the creative arts and are committed to nurturing talent, encouraging participation, and celebrating achievement. Through this, we ensure that every child has the opportunity to shine creatively and develop a deep appreciation for the arts
Brass Tuition
This year we are delighted to be recipients of funding from The Humphrey Taylor Richardson Charitable Trust.
Their support has enabled us to team up with Surrey Arts to provide brass instruction to Year 4 , 5 and 6 this year.
We are looking forward to developing the 'Trinity Oaks Brass Band'.

pageCache.pageTitle: Early Years EYFS (Reception 4-5 years) | Begin Learning Today — Enroll Now — Trinity Oaks CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Early Years EYFS (Reception 4-5 years)
The Early Years Foundation Stage Curriculum
The Foundation Stage includes Acorns pre-school and Apple Reception class. Teachers work together to plan teaching and learning opportunities. We value and want to build upon the children’s previous experiences both from home and nursery settings. In the children’s first term of Reception we aim to make the transition from any previous setting as smooth and consistent as possible.
Through exploring different aspects of a theme children will experience all areas of the Foundation Stage Curriculum to build their vital foundational knowledge. When they begin school, the children will work towards the Department for Education (DfE) “Early Learning Goals” within the EYFS Curriculum which covers the following prime areas:
Communication and Language
Physical Development
Personal, Social and Emotional Development
There are also 4 specific areas, through which the three prime areas are strengthened and applied. These are:
Understanding the world
Expressive arts and design
The children will experience these areas of the curriculum through both indoor and outdoor environments; we strongly believe that children learn through their play and by offering a range of different stimulating environments we allow the children to enhance their learning experience and development.
The children follow a curriculum which is based around topics and themes which will engage the children and be led by their interests.
If you would like to learn more about our curriculum, please contact us.

School Tours
Welcome to Trinity Oaks CofE Primary School
I am delighted that you are interested in seeing what we have to offer your child as they start their Primary School journey.
As a school, we pride our selves on our strong relationships and sense of community and as you tour the school you are invited to go into classrooms and get a real feel for the school.
Trinity Oaks is a one-form-entry through Primary School with a teacher-led pre-school - so we have children from the term after they are three years old right up to Year 6, when the children are turning 11 and preparing to head off to secondary (I know that this feels a long way off for you right now!). We are a small school which enables children to foster and develop close relationships with all the adults and children in the school - we are a family.
As you make your choice for your child’s first school experience it is vital that you feel that your choices are the best for your child - please ask any questions as you tour the school.
We look forward to meeting you meeting you.
Mrs Woods - Headteacher

pageCache.text:
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities
At Trinity Oaks, every child is cherished, valued and known as an individual. Rooted in our Christian vision, “Where acorns flourish into mighty oaks”, we are committed to ensuring that all pupils, including those with special educational needs or disabilities (SEND), feel loved, included and supported to thrive academically, socially and emotionally.
‍We believe that all children can succeed, and we work in partnership with families to remove barriers to learning, nurture strengths and celebrate the unique qualities that each child brings to our school.
‍Our Inclusive Approach
‍A pupil has SEND if they require provision that is additional to or different from what is typically available to pupils their age, in line with the SEND Code of Practice (2015).
Our inclusive culture ensures that most needs are met within our rich, high‑quality classroom teaching, supplemented by targeted support when required. Where appropriate this is supported by targeted and personalised provision, reviewed regularly using the graduated approach of Assess-Plan-Do-Review.
‍We support children across all four recognised areas of SEND:
Communication & Interaction
Cognition & Learning
Social, Emotional & Mental Health
Sensory and/or Physical Needs
How We Support Children With SEND
All teachers at Trinity Oaks are teachers of SEND. Provision is overseen by our SENCo & Assistant Head (Inclusion):
Mrs Alice Price – senco@trinityoaks.surrey.sch.uk
Warm, Welcoming Partnership With Families
If you have concerns, your first point of contact is your child’s class teacher, or you may contact the SENCo directly. We promise to listen with kindness, work collaboratively, and ensure clear shared outcomes.
Inclusion Beyond the Classroom
Children with SEND are fully included in clubs, trips, events and wider opportunities. Adjustments are thoughtfully planned so every child can participate confidently and safely.

pageCache.text:
Worship and Prayer
Worship is an integral part of our day where the whole school gather to reflect on both the school values and British Values. Links are made to develop the children’s Biblical understanding while exploring how our values impact on our, and other, lives. Teachers regularly discuss the school values in class, to enable the children to gain a deeper understanding and to reflect on and apply the values in their daily lives and learning.
In order to support the whole school, worship is also planned to reflect the diversity of our community. We recognise the main festivals of the cultures represented in the school and children are encouraged to share their faith with others. Every child is valued and every faith is valued – we look for similarities and shared experiences.
Our worships follow the structure of gather, engage, respond and send.
We gather together and greet each other. We all come to play a part in this community. We are preparing to meet God.
We engage with the big things and the little things in life. We encounter Jesus and the stories of the Bible. We are listening for God’s message for us.
We respond to what we have heard and seen. We respond together as individuals. We are given the opportunity to worship God.
We are sent out to love and serve one another and to make a difference in the world. We are all dismissed with God’s blessing.
At Trinity Oaks all children are invited to pray to God. Where children prefer not to pray to God, they are encouraged to respect the values of other and use the time to reflect on their own thoughts.
Prayer is used as an opportunity to speak to God and give thanks for his many blessings. Prayer at Trinity Oaks links to spirituality and recognising God’s hand our lives.
At the beginning of every worship children are called to worship using a invitation.
‘Jesus light of the world is here, Lord Jesus shine in us… Amen’
This is then followed by the school prayer:
Let peace live here,
Let the rooms be full of happiness,
Let love be all around.
Love for one another,
Love for life itself,
That as many hands build a house,
So many hearts make a school.
Both of these prayers are signed using Makaton - this ensures inclusivity for all.
We have an allocated prayer space on entry to the school and children are encouraged to contribute their prayers to this space - talking with God is part of our spirituality offer and, alongside the child led faith group, children are supported to give thanks to God for the wonderful world in which they live as well as seek guidance and help for any challenges that they or others are facing.
